CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFLDAP

CFLDAP talks to a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) server, such as a company phone book. ACTION="Query" searches the directory and returns the entries as a query object, one column per attribute, so you can display them with CFOUTPUT just like database rows. ACTION="Add", "Modify", "ModifyDN" and "Delete" change the directory.

KoldFusion speaks LDAP version 3 itself, without a directory SDK, and ships with its own directory server, the Gibson Directory Server. It runs on the same machine as KoldFusion (port 3890 unless the Administrator says otherwise, see Miscellaneous > Directory Server) and holds the employees of the Gibson Mainframe Co. below the base DN o=Gibson Mainframe Co, c=US. The variables Server.Directory.Host, Server.Directory.Port and Server.Directory.BaseDN tell your pages where to find it.

Category

Internet protocols

Syntax

<CFLDAP SERVER="server_name"
    PORT="port_number"
    USERNAME="name"
    PASSWORD="password"
    ACTION="action"
    NAME="name"
    TIMEOUT="seconds"
    MAXROWS="number"
    START="distinguished_name"
    SCOPE="scope"
    ATTRIBUTES="attribute, attribute"
    FILTER="filter"
    SORT="attribute[, attribute]..."
    SORTCONTROL="nocase, asc|desc"
    DN="distinguished_name"
    STARTROW="row_number"
    MODIFYTYPE="replace|add|delete"
    REBIND="Yes|No"
    REFERRAL="number_of_hops"
    SEPARATOR="separator_character"
    DELIMITER="delimiter_character">

Attributes

SERVER
Required. Host name or IP address of the LDAP server. For the built-in directory use #Server.Directory.Host#.
PORT
Optional, default "389". TCP port of the LDAP server. The built-in directory listens on #Server.Directory.Port# (3890 by default).
USERNAME
Optional. Distinguished name to bind (log in) as, for example "cn=Directory Manager". Without it the tag binds anonymously, which is enough to search most directories but not to change them.
PASSWORD
Optional. Password of USERNAME.
ACTION
Optional, default "Query". Query, Add, Modify, ModifyDN or Delete.
NAME
Required for Query. Name of the query object that receives the entries.
TIMEOUT
Optional, default "60". Seconds to wait for the server.
MAXROWS
Optional. Maximum number of entries to return.
START
Required for Query. Distinguished name of the entry where the search starts, such as "ou=People, o=Gibson Mainframe Co, c=US".
SCOPE
Optional, default "OneLevel". OneLevel (the entries directly below START), Base (START itself) or Subtree (START and everything below it).
ATTRIBUTES
Required for Query, Add, Modify, ModifyDN. For Query, a comma-separated list of the attributes to return; each becomes a column (characters that are not allowed in column names become underscores). "*" returns every attribute plus a DN column; "dn" in the list adds the DN column. For Add and Modify, a list of name=value pairs separated by DELIMITER (a semicolon); several values for one attribute are separated by SEPARATOR (a comma). For ModifyDN, the new relative distinguished name, such as "uid=bjensen".
FILTER
Optional, default "objectclass=*". LDAP search filter (RFC 2254): (attribute=value), wildcards (sn=S*), presence (mail=*), (cn~=sound-alike), (employeeNumber>=10), (employeeNumber<=10) and the combinations (&...) (|...) (!...). Use \2a, \28, \29 and \5c for a literal *, (, ) and \.
SORT
Optional. Comma-separated attributes to sort the entries by; each may be followed by ASC or DESC. KoldFusion sorts the results itself, as the 4.5 server did, so it works with any directory.
SORTCONTROL
Optional, default "asc". nocase (case-insensitive), asc and desc, combined with commas, as in "nocase, desc".
DN
Required for Add, Modify, ModifyDN, Delete. Distinguished name of the entry to change.
STARTROW
Optional, default "1". First entry to return; use with MAXROWS to page through results.
MODIFYTYPE
Optional, default "Replace". For Modify: Replace the attribute's values, Add values to it, or Delete values (give "name=" with no value to delete the whole attribute).
REBIND
Optional, default "No". Yes binds to referred servers with USERNAME and PASSWORD; No binds anonymously.
REFERRAL
Optional, default "0". Number of referral hops to follow; 0 does not follow referrals.
SEPARATOR
Optional, default ",". Separates the values of a multi-valued attribute in ATTRIBUTES (Add, Modify). In query results multi-valued attributes are joined with ", " unless SEPARATOR is given.
DELIMITER
Optional, default ";". Separates the name=value pairs in ATTRIBUTES (Add, Modify).

Usage

Query results have the usual RecordCount, CurrentRow and ColumnList variables. An attribute with several values, such as objectClass, shows them joined with commas: "top, person, inetOrgPerson".

Because SEPARATOR splits values at commas, a value that contains a comma (such as "l=Boston, MA") needs another separator: SEPARATOR="|" ATTRIBUTES="objectclass=top|person;l=Boston, MA".

Errors are thrown as Application exceptions you can catch with CFCATCH TYPE="Any". The message carries the LDAP result code, for example "An error has occured while trying to execute query :[LDAP: error code 32 - No Such Object]", and CFCATCH.ErrorCode holds the number (32). A server that cannot be reached gives "Connection to LDAP server failed."

CFLDAP can be disabled for ordinary templates on the Basic Security page of the Administrator.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- Who works in Engineering? Ask the Gibson Directory Server --->
<CFLDAP ACTION="Query" NAME="People"
        SERVER="#Server.Directory.Host#" PORT="#Server.Directory.Port#"
        START="ou=People, #Server.Directory.BaseDN#" SCOPE="OneLevel"
        FILTER="(&(objectclass=person)(ou=Engineering))"
        ATTRIBUTES="cn,title,mail,telephoneNumber" SORT="cn" SORTCONTROL="nocase">
<CFOUTPUT><P>#People.RecordCount# people work in Engineering.</P></CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Name</TH><TH>Title</TH><TH>E-mail</TH><TH>Phone</TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="People">
<TR><TD>#cn#</TD><TD>#title#</TD><TD>#mail#</TD><TD>#telephoneNumber#</TD></TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
<!--- Errors carry the LDAP result code --->
<CFTRY>
  <CFLDAP ACTION="Query" NAME="Nobody" SERVER="#Server.Directory.Host#" PORT="#Server.Directory.Port#"
          START="ou=Nowhere, #Server.Directory.BaseDN#" ATTRIBUTES="cn">
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Any">
    <CFOUTPUT><P><B>#CFCATCH.Message#</B> (ErrorCode #CFCATCH.ErrorCode#)</P></CFOUTPUT>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
